proposed_from.topic: Design-stage minimax admissibility frontier for an external prognostic score of unknown quality. Finite population of n even units with FIXED potential outcomes; randomness is the assignment alone (design-based). Estimand SATE, estimator the design-unbiased difference-in-means, so with mu_i=(y_i(1)+y_i(0))/2 the exact risk is (4/n^2) mu' A_d mu where A_d=Cov_d(z). Design class D_n: all distributions on {z in {-1,+1}^n : sum z_i = 0} with E[z]=0, so A_d>=0, diag(A_d)=1, A_d*1=0; it contains complete randomization, every score-based stratified, matched-pair and rerandomization scheme, and all their mixtures. An external prognostic score, known for every unit BEFORE randomization and possibly miscalibrated or population-shifted, gives a fixed score subspace S (its score-derived span intersected with 1-perp), a PRIMITIVE known exactly at design time, with 1 <= dim S <= n-1. Score-quality class Y(rho,M;S) = {mu : ||mu||^2 = nM, ||P_S mu||^2 >= rho^2 ||mu||^2}; rho is UNKNOWN at design time (GSW JASA 2024 Sec 8: the analogous quantity 'cannot be directly observed or estimated in the design stage'). Determine V*(rho;S) := inf over d in D_n of sup over Y(rho,M;S) of mu' A_d mu, with an attaining design AND a matching converse over the full class D_n; and characterize the admissibility dichotomy A_n := {S : V*(rho;S) < V_CRD(rho;S) for some rho < 1} together with the threshold rho*(S) := inf{rho : V*(rho;S) < V_CRD(rho;S)} (=1 off A_n), including whether that characterization is computable from the score matrix alone. Also determine the finite-n additive regret R*(n,S) of a single design chosen without knowing rho. The unindexed minimax is degenerate (GSW Prop 4.2; Kapelner JSPI 2022 Sec 3.1); the score-quality indexing is what makes it nondegenerate. Exact enumerated witnesses: at n=8 with the pair-partition S, the matched-pair design has risk exactly 1.75x complete randomization on a legal mu that varies within pairs and risk 0 on one constant within pairs, so V*(1;S)=0<V_CRD(1;S)=4/7 and S is in A_n; and S=1-perp is NOT in A_n because trace n on an (n-1)-dimensional space forces lambda_max >= n/(n-1) with equality only at complete randomization. Functional forms, the value of rho*(S), the attaining design (pure or mixed), and any asymptotic formulation are delegated.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: {"published_axis":"The closest published results are HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 and Kallus2021Randomization. The former gives separate finite-sample balance and robustness bounds for a named algorithm, not an exact oracle over all balanced assignment laws indexed by score quality. Kallus2021Randomization, Section 5, supplies the generic mixed-strategy minimax criterion and an ellipsoidal largest-eigenvalue example; that architecture informs the outer game. The strict theorem-level delta is an exact rank-one lift for the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell, a saddle program over the true fixed-count balanced cut hull, recovery of an attaining sign-pair design with a full-class converse, and the if-and-only-if invariants \\(\\kappa(S)\\) and \\(\\gamma(S)\\). HuberMaric2019, p. 5, Theorem 2, supplies the Bernoulli cut-polytope geometry but no fixed-count causal-risk objective.","repository_axis":"The nearest accepted repository proposal, exp\\_design\\_pm1\\_exactness\\_boundary\\_v1, studies implementability loss for a different interference objective and explicitly leaves its exact zero-versus-positive frontier open. It does not contain a prognostic score-quality shell, the rank-one-exact two-constraint lift, the admissibility dichotomy, or unknown-quality regret. The present kernel uses the prior review lesson that a positive semidefinite optimizer is not enough: every covariance is optimized directly in the convex hull of balanced sign outer products."}
seed_list: Exact balanced-hypercube saddle program for the score-quality minimax risk, with an attaining mixed assignment law and a converse over every balanced mean-zero design.
Necessary-and-sufficient score-subspace admissibility certificate and a critical quality threshold computable from the score matrix.
Finite-population minimax regret of one design selected before score quality is known.
Risk versus exact-randomization-inference frontier under a cap on the probability of every assignment.
Matched-pair critical-quality formula for a pair-partition score space, including the point where within-pair misspecification reverses the ranking against complete randomization.
Complexity boundary for deciding score-subspace admissibility from a rational score matrix.
Monotonicity and failure of monotonicity of admissibility when the score span is enlarged by additional prognostic features.
Growing-score-dimension phase diagram linking finite-population admissibility to asymptotic robustness of balanced designs.

seed_details.one_line: Derive an exact semidefinite saddle representation of the score-quality minimax risk over the full balanced assignment polytope and recover an attaining assignment mixture from its dual.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024, Section 8 of the supplement, states that the relevant residual-to-total predictive ratio cannot be observed or estimated at the design stage; its Introduction and Conclusion frame the unresolved balance-versus-robustness choice.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from the mixed-strategy optimal-design definition in Kallus2021Randomization because the adversary is merely another outcome class.
seed_details.rebuttal: The abstract minimax definition does not remove the rank constraint created by the spherical quality cone, does not enforce realizability in the balanced cut hull, and gives neither the exact lifted dual nor the score-specific saddle certificate.

seed_details.one_line: Characterize score spaces admitting improvement before perfect prediction by an if-and-only-if compressed-eigenvalue certificate, and express the critical quality as a scalar spectral ratio over realizable assignment covariances.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 provides separate balance and robustness guarantees but does not locate the finite-sample transition for an arbitrary score span; HuberMaric2019 shows why positive semidefiniteness alone cannot certify a genuine binary assignment law.
seed_details.referee_objection: The threshold is tautological because it is defined as the first quality level at which the value improves.
seed_details.rebuttal: The proposed result eliminates the nested risk optimization and replaces it with the explicit invariant \(\gamma(S)\), while the separate condition \(\kappa(S)<n/(n-1)\) is an if-and-only-if certificate evaluated entirely in the balanced cut hull.

seed_details.one_line: Choose one balanced assignment law before \(\rho\) is known and minimize its worst additive loss relative to the \(\rho\)-specific oracle.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024, Section 8, exposes the unavailable quality input, while KapelnerKriegerSklarAzriel2022, Section 3.1 and Discussion, shows that existing rerandomization tuning depends on unknown response quantities.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a routine robust-optimization epigraph once the oracle value is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: The subtraction of a quality-indexed oracle and the continuum of nonellipsoidal adversary classes create a nontrivial spectral-breakpoint problem for a single covariance in the discrete feasible hull.

seed_details.one_line: Impose \(\max_z d(z)\le \alpha/2\) and derive the exact score-quality risk cost of retaining a nontrivial Fisher randomization test.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Kallus2021Randomization, Introduction and Concluding Remarks, separates precision-optimal mixing from the assignment uniformity required for design-based testing.
seed_details.referee_objection: Kallus2021Randomization already adds exactly this coordinatewise mass constraint.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection defeats this as a standalone first version: replacing an ellipsoid by the score-quality cone changes the value but not the conceptual kernel.

seed_details.one_line: For a fixed pair partition, derive the exact critical quality at which matched-pair randomization first beats complete randomization despite adversarial within-pair variation.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Bai2022MatchedPairs, Introduction and Discussion, establishes matched-pair optimality within stratified superpopulation designs but leaves design-stage performance dependent on an unknown prognostic index.
seed_details.referee_objection: The pair-partition spectrum makes this a short exercise once the general quality class is written down.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection largely holds; the pair case is retained only as a mandatory reduction and diagnostic for the arbitrary-subspace theorem.

seed_details.one_line: Classify the computational complexity of deciding whether a rational score matrix generates an admissible subspace, with exact separation oracles for tractable score geometries.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: HuberMaric2019, Introduction and Discussion, identifies binary correlation feasibility with cut-polytope membership; its design implication is that ordinary semidefinite covariance constraints are insufficient.
seed_details.referee_objection: Cut-polytope membership and related binary quadratic programs are already known to be hard, so the complexity result may be inherited without new causal content.
seed_details.rebuttal: The precise decision problem quantifies a compressed spectral optimum rather than membership of a supplied covariance, but a hardness theorem alone would still be too remote from the design consumer.

seed_details.one_line: Determine when enlarging a prognostic score span preserves, creates, or destroys minimax admissibility.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: SchulerWalshHallWalshFisher2022, Introduction and Discussion, emphasizes that external-score gains depend on transported predictive accuracy and can vanish under population shift.
seed_details.referee_objection: Subspace inclusion should make this a routine monotonicity argument.
seed_details.rebuttal: The quality class itself changes under enlargement, so monotonicity need not follow; nevertheless the economic content is secondary to the exact admissibility certificate.

seed_details.one_line: Derive an asymptotic phase diagram for admissibility when both the score rank and the balanced assignment geometry vary with \(n\).
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024, Conclusion, shows asymptotic escape from the balance-robustness trade-off for its Gram--Schmidt design, while its exact-balance modification falls outside the main analysis.
seed_details.referee_objection: An asymptotic formulation would conceal rather than solve the finite balanced-hypercube obstruction.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for a first version; asymptotics become meaningful only after the finite \(n\) value and certificate are established.

proposed_from.literature_map: Harshaw, Sävje, Spielman, and Zhang (2024), Introduction, Sections 3--4, Section 8 of the supplement, and Conclusion, provide the exact assignment-covariance risk identity and the balance--robustness motivation, but state that the residual-to-total predictive ratio cannot be observed or estimated when the design is chosen. Kallus (2018), Introduction and Sections 2--4, supplies the zero-sum design formulation and optimization over randomized balanced partitions; Kallus (2021), Introduction, Section 2, and Concluding Remarks, clarifies that the mixed-strategy design is the minimax object and that permutation-symmetric classes return complete randomization. Huber and Marić (2019), Introduction, Theorem 3, and Discussion, identify feasible symmetric-Bernoulli correlations with a cut-polytope image, which prevents replacing the assignment hull by the elliptope. Bai (2022), Introduction, oracle-design section, and Discussion, gives the closest scalar-prognosis endpoint but optimizes only within stratified superpopulation schemes. Kapelner, Krieger, Sklar, and Azriel (2022), Section 3.1 and Discussion, optimize a rerandomization threshold using unknown response features and leave the difference-in-means version unresolved. Hu, Zhu, Brunskill, and Wager (2024), Introduction and Discussion, provide the adjacent oracle-relative minimax-regret game for trial enrollment, but not for assignment covariances or a continuum of score qualities. Schuler, Walsh, Hall, Walsh, and Fisher (2022), Introduction and Discussion, show why an externally trained prognostic score can lose its value under population shift. Schindl and Branson (2024), Introduction and Discussion, optimize within quadratic-form rerandomization and explicitly do not compare that class with other assignment strategies. Guo, Liang, and Toulis (2025), Introduction, design-optimization section, and Conclusion, state that full binary covariance optimization is cut-polytope hard and instead optimize a restricted Gaussianized class locally. No located paper studies the nested shell \(\|P_S\mu\|^2\geq \rho^2\|\mu\|^2\), its exact balanced-cut-hull value, or the resulting admissibility threshold.
